source: KE = ½mv², so doubling the speed gives four times the energy.
Students think doubling the speed doubles the kinetic energy.

Every moving thing has kinetic energy, the form of energy that comes with motion. A faster or heavier object has more. The formula has a square in it, so you will need the order of operations: square the speed first, then multiply.
$$\text{KE} = \tfrac{1}{2}\,m\,v^2$$ with mass in kg and speed in m/s, giving joules. Because the speed is squared, doubling the speed makes the kinetic energy four times as big.

Why squared? To speed something up, you push it through a distance, and a faster object covers more distance during each push. Getting from 0 to 20 m/s takes four times the energy of getting from 0 to 10 m/s, not twice. That is also why a car at highway speed needs about four times the braking distance it needs at half that speed.
Kinetic energy of a 2 kg ball against its speed. At 5 m/s it has 25 J; at 10 m/s, 100 J. Twice the speed, four times the energy.
Find the kinetic energy of a 2 kg ball rolling at 3 m/s.
A 1,000 kg car moves at 20 m/s. Find its kinetic energy, then find it again at 40 m/s.
Twice the speed gives $2^2 = 4$ times the energy.

Thinking that doubling the speed doubles the kinetic energy. The speed is squared, so it multiplies the energy by $2^2 = 4$; tripling the speed multiplies it by 9. Check: in your work, the speed should be squared before anything else is multiplied.
